messages:
Maya: Quick FYI — running a prelaunch capacity probe for Orbiter-30B. Synthetic traffic from our EU staging cluster is showing ~4.2k tokens/sec per GPU shard under the default batching config. We need a stopgap estimate for GPU-hours and a mitigation plan if this holds in canary.
Sanjay: Can you paste the perf snapshot? which sequence lengths + batch sizes?
Maya: seq dist is heavy: p95 ~ 512, p99 ~ 1.2k. Using batching: dynamic batch with max_batch_size=64, max_latency_ms=40. Perf sample: "
Maya: ```
Shard 1: 4,180 tok/s
Shard 2: 4,050 tok/s
KV hit ratio: 0.14
Avg latency (token gen): 42ms
GPU utl: 86%
```
Liam: If that's stable, each shard = ~15 GPU-hours per 1M tokens? roughly. Need to translate into committed capacity for a 24h canary and peak hour headroom.
Hana: Also note EU-west has the 2x network egress throttles on the BC cluster this week (ticket #INC-4321), so we should assume ~10% headroom loss for cross-AZ RPCs.
deploy-bot: Canary job started: orbiter-30b/canary-2026-03-15 - 6 pods, autoscale=min 6,max 24.
Sanjay: Quick calc: at 4.2k tok/s per shard * 6 shards = 25.2k tok/s sustained. Over a 1-hour peak -> ~90M tokens. Multiply by our cost model => ~GPU-hours = 6 shards * 1 hour + kernel inefficiencies = ~6.8 GPU-hours/hour. For 3-hour sustained peak, ~20.4 GPU-hours.
Maya: So 24h canary with daily diurnal peak (3h) => baseline 24*6 = 144 GPU-hours + 20.4 extra during peak -> ~164 GPU-hours. Add 20% safety -> ~197 GPU-hours.
Hana: Can we reduce token/sec via config tweaks? suggestions: smaller max_batch_size (32) or reduce max_latency_ms to bias for lower tail latency. Also enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts.
Liam: Tradeoffs: smaller batch -> lower throughput per GPU -> need more shards -> higher GPU-hours. But reduces tail latency and may reduce KV pressure. Try setting max_batch_size=48 and enable prefix cache; run A/B for 1h.
Maya: I'll kick an A/B with {max_batch_size:48, prefix_cache:on} vs current. Expect delta in tok/s and KV hit. Can someone reserve 4 extra GPUs in eu-west for the next 2 hours?
ops-oncall: I can spin up 4 p4d-equivalent instances in eu-west. ETA ~18m. Note: if we hit 24 total pods autoscale may exhaust quota -> will patch quota now.
Sanjay: Also flag: if network egress hits thresholds, we should route to eu-south fallback region. That adds latency but keeps availability. Need a routing policy update in the next 12h.
Maya: Agree — plan: 1) reserve 4 GPUs now 2) run A/B for 1h 3) collect tok/s, p95/p99, kv-hit, cost delta 4) reconvene. If A/B worse -> fallback to current and open rollback.
Hana: For forecasting sheet: please append projected GPU-hours for a 7-day ramp scenario: start=200 GPU-hours/day, +30% day-over-day for 3 days, plateau. I'll update cost model with reserved vs on-demand delta.
Liam: Quick note on billing: reserved capacity gives ~35% discount vs on-demand for committed 3mo. If expected sustained >120 GPU-hours/day then discuss a short commitment.
Maya: Thanks — tagging @ops-oncall when canary A/B data lands. Will post perf CSV and small analysis. :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: Quota patched, 4 instances provisioning. Canary A/B job expected to start within 20m.
Maya: Uploaded initial perf CSV to the thread: https://internal.redwood/att/orbiter_canary_030526.csv - raw numbers only.
Sanjay: Received. I'll run the cost/provisioning simulation and post numbers in ~40m.
Liam: If we see tok/s drop <10% with caching on -> we can avoid +8 GPUs and save ~160 GPU-hours over 7 days.
Maya: Great. Will close loop after A/B. If anyone sees latency >120ms p99, abort canary and rollback to previous model variant.
Hana: noted. Filing a lightweight runbook for the rollback path now.
